policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 5 Jun close (1x4 3.88, 3x6 4.04, 6x9 4.34, 9x12 4.55 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 70bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. May minutes (5 Jun): the CPI outlook is highly uncertain even short term and hinges on fuel prices and the fuel measures; most members backed the hold. May flash CPI 3.1% (29 May; 3.7% expected, -0.3% m/m on food); core 3.0% in April. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 June (extended 28 May).
policy.risk_text: The MPC turned dovish (Glapiński, 3 Jun: no reason to change or even discuss rates), so FRAs trade oil and the Iran talks; risks: renewed Gulf fighting and the fuel package ending (excise from 15 Jun) lifting CPI; long end: the 17 and 24 Jun sales and the deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after April PLN 89.3bn (30.1% of the limit); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; windfall-tax bill (75% of margins above the 2025 level +20%) in preparation; fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps, minimum excise) to 15 June (28 May).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~56% (MoF, 29 May) financed; budget accounts >PLN 200bn expected at end-May (Drop, 29 May); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P affirmed A-/stable (8 May) and its analyst calls the missing medium-term consolidation the key rating risk (26 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 5-7 Jun: May MPC minutes: the CPI outlook is highly uncertain even short term and hinges on fuel prices and the fuel measures; a further CPI rise was possible; some members flagged wage risks; most backed the hold. Millennium: before Glapinski ~1 hike by year-end and ~2 in 12 months were priced. NBP reserves rose to EUR 255.6bn. POLGB yields rose ~6-12bp on the week (PKO) and edged up on Friday ahead of US payrolls. Abroad: payrolls +172k (85k expected) made a 25bp Fed hike by year-end almost fully priced (December 63%); UST10 >4.5%, Nasdaq's worst day in a year, EUR/USD 1.153; euro-area Q1 GDP revised to -0.2% q/q; Reuters poll: ECB to 2.25% on 11 June. Weekend: IRGC strikes on US bases, US strikes on Iranian radars, Israel hit Beirut; Iran plans Hormuz fees; OPEC+ +188k b/d; Burnham to challenge Starmer.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 17 Jun, 24 Jun. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: talks stalled and Gulf clashes resumed - Brent back at ~$95-98; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 70bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike, the BoE is priced for hikes, the CNB is on hold and the MNB is on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 51bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 276bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 5 Jun close). Payrolls +172k; Fed hike by Dec priced (5-7 Jun).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun (8Y EUR 1.25bn, 15Y EUR 0.75bn; demand EUR 4.6bn); FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
